concepts.label: curse of dimensionality — corpus extension evidence
K-Means is the default, most-used clustering algorithm
The K-Means algorithm cycle: iteratively assign points to the nearest centroid, recompute centroids as the mean of assigned points, repeat until assignments stop changing
K-Means minimizes the within-cluster sum of squared distances to centroids (inertia / WCSS)
K-Means is sensitive to centroid initialization (poor starts converge to suboptimal solutions)
K-Means assumes roughly spherical clusters of similar size (Euclidean geometry limitation)
Choosing K with the elbow method: plot inertia/WCSS against K and take the diminishing-returns bend as the optimal K
DBSCAN: density-based clustering — clusters are high-density regions separated by low-density regions; handles arbitrary shapes and flags outliers as noise
Hierarchical clustering builds a tree of clusters (dendrogram)
Clustering is the unsupervised task of discovering groups in unlabeled data (vs. supervised classification with predefined classes)
Outliers and clustering: K-Means' mean-based weakness to outliers (course) vs. clustering as an anomaly-detection tool (master-ai)
Dimensionality reduction projects high-dimensional data to a lower-dimensional space while preserving structure; PCA is the linear approach, t-SNE/UMAP the non-linear ones
PCA projects data onto the directions of maximum variance, preserving as much variance as possible
PCA captures only linear, global structure and misses non-linear and local structure (use t-SNE/UMAP/autoencoders for those)
Standardize features before PCA (and before t-SNE/UMAP): large-scale features dominate otherwise
Dimensionality reduction's use-case portfolio: visualization, compression/denoising, and preprocessing for downstream models
PCA as preprocessing speeds up downstream algorithms (e.g. clustering), at a cost
Choosing the number of PCA components: acknowledged by master-ai as PCA's one knob, worked out by the course via explained variance
PCA outputs are hard to interpret: components are mixtures of all features (course) and PCA preprocessing sacrifices interpretability (master-ai)
t-SNE: non-linear reduction built for 2D/3D visualization that preserves local structure but not global structure
t-SNE misuse guidance: use it only for visualization — not for downstream modeling, not for interpreting inter-cluster distances, not for choosing K or clustering
Perplexity as t-SNE's key hyperparameter: named in master-ai's worked example, explained (range, local/global effect, try-multiple advice) only by the course
UMAP's advantage profile over t-SNE: faster, preserves global structure better, and can embed new points for preprocessing/downstream use
UMAP's two meaningful hyperparameters n_neighbors and min_dist — and that they matter (don't use defaults blindly)
Determinism profile across the three methods: PCA deterministic, t-SNE stochastic (different runs give different plots), UMAP deterministic/reproducible
Method-selection guidance across PCA / t-SNE / UMAP (and autoencoders): visualization vs preprocessing vs non-linear end-to-end
Visualizing embeddings from trained models (word2vec/BERT/ViT or text/image embeddings) with UMAP/t-SNE as the standard inspection practice
Autoencoders as the neural / non-linear alternative to PCA for dimensionality reduction (defined by master-ai; pointed to by the course from both DR notes)
